content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): lifts the 15:30-17:30 service level to 98.5% against an 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The payments spike is driven by the UPI timeout outage (P1 incident INC-20261010-3825), with upi_payment_failed calls at 4x normal. Service level has already recovered to 100% at 15:15 because staffing rose to 41 agents against 31 planned. Doing nothing is predicted to hold 94.8% over the window (payments 92.5%), so we are already above target. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It moves 8 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 16:00-17:00, delays payments breaks by 30 min, and adds IVR callback. This raises payments to 98.4% while general stays at 98.7%. Abandons fall from 1.5% to 0.4%, and rest-of-day service level improves from 92.7% to 94.8%.","trade_offs":["Versus P0 (no action, INR 0): P0 already meets target at 94.8%, but payments is thinner at 92.5% and abandons are 1.5%. P1 adds headroom for no cost.","Versus P2 (INR 570): P2 reaches 99.8% and 0.1% abandons. It also tackles the outage directly with an IVR outage message and chat deflection. The gain is small for the spend.","Versus P3 (INR 3,450): P3 gives 100% and 96.6% rest of day, but uses overtime that isn't needed at current levels.","Risk to general: moving 8 agents leaves general at a predicted 98.7%, which is still comfortable. Delayed breaks put some extra load on payments agents."],"watch":"Watch the UPI incident status and the volume of upi_payment_failed calls. If the outage drags on past 17:00 or volumes climb again, consider switching to P2 so the outage IVR message and deflection can absorb repeat status enquiries. Also check general queue service level while the 8 agents are moved."}
